Multnomah County operates two primary adult detention facilities, the Multnomah County Detention Center (MCDC) and the Inverness Jail (IJ). The provided information primarily pertains to MCDC, which is located in downtown Portland.

If you need to locate an inmate in Multnomah County, Oregon, there are several official resources and procedures available to help you find current information. Whether you're searching for someone held in the county jail or need to understand the booking process, this guide covers everything you need to know about conducting a multnomah county oregon inmate lookup. The Multnomah County Sheriff's Office maintains records of all individuals currently in custody and provides public access to this information through multiple channels.

How to Search Multnomah County Jail Records

  1. Visit the official Multnomah County Sheriff's Office website or use their online inmate search tool to access real-time custody information.
  2. Enter the inmate's first and last name into the search database. You may also search by booking number if you have that information available.
  3. Review the search results, which will display the inmate's current status, charges, custody location, and booking date.
  4. Note the inmate's booking number and facility location for reference when contacting the jail or arranging visitation.
  5. If the person is not located in Multnomah County custody, check the Oregon Department of Corrections Inmate Locator for state prison records.
  6. For individuals in federal custody, use the Federal Bureau of Prisons Inmate Locator to confirm their current location and status.
  7. Keep your search results and reference numbers handy when making phone inquiries or scheduling visits to the facility.

Bail Bond Information for Multnomah County

When someone is arrested in Multnomah County, they may be eligible for bail or release on their own recognizance, depending on the charges and their background. A bail bondsman can help secure an inmate's release by posting bail on their behalf. The standard fee for a bail bondsman in Oregon is typically 10 percent of the total bail amount, though this may vary based on the specific bail bond company and circumstances of the case. This fee is non-refundable and represents the cost of the bonding service. Once a bail bond has been posted, the inmate may be released from custody pending their court appearance.

The arraignment typically occurs within 72 hours of arrest in Multnomah County. At the arraignment, the judge will review charges, set or adjust bail amounts, and explain the defendant's rights and responsibilities. It is important to arrange bail bond services quickly after an arrest, as delayed payment can result in extended jail stays. Family members or the inmate themselves can contact licensed bail bond agents in Multnomah County to discuss options and begin the release process immediately after booking is complete.

Visitation Rules at Multnomah County Jail

  • Identification: All visitors must present a valid government-issued photo ID at the entrance of the facility.
  • Visiting Hours: Standard visitation hours are typically Tuesday through Sunday during designated times. Contact the jail directly to confirm current visiting hours.
  • Dress Code: Visitors must wear appropriate clothing. No revealing garments, transparent clothing, or items depicting gang affiliations are permitted.
  • Video Visitation: Remote video visits are available for those unable to visit in person. These visits can be arranged through the facility's designated video visitation system.
  • Children Policy: Children under 18 are permitted to visit but must be supervised by a responsible adult at all times during the visit.

What to Expect After Arrest in Multnomah County

  1. Booking: After arrest, the inmate is brought to the booking area where personal information, charges, and background details are recorded into the system. This process typically takes one to two hours.
  2. Medical Screening: A medical evaluation is performed to assess the inmate's health status and identify any urgent medical needs or mental health concerns.
  3. Classification: Staff determine the inmate's custody level and appropriate housing assignment based on charges, background, and security risk assessment.
  4. Arraignment: The inmate appears before a judge within 72 hours for an initial hearing where bail is set and rights are explained.
  5. Transfer: Depending on bail status and case progression, the inmate may be transferred to the appropriate housing unit or released pending further court dates.

How to Contact Multnomah County Jail

For inquiries about an inmate's custody status, visitation scheduling, or other jail-related questions, you can contact the Multnomah County Sheriff's Office directly. Multiple contact methods are available to serve your needs, including phone lines dedicated to inmate information and visitation coordination. Having the inmate's full name and booking number will help facilitate faster information retrieval when you call.
